tweets.text: 🇬🇧 British Army’s Ajax vehicles broke down again after coming out of storage. Several of the £6.3bn armoured vehicles developed faults during trials after sitting unused for eight months. A captain even warned that some were “unsuitable for operations” but the response was basically “make do.” Apparently Ajax can handle everything except a little downtime. Impressive. Source: RT News / Writer: Lynn

tweets.creator: @MarioNawfal
tweets.text: 🇨🇺 Trump admin is turning up the heat on Cuba and quietly looking for someone new to run Havana. Washington wants the island to open its economy, let in more U.S. businesses, buy American oil, and dial back the Russian and Chinese intelligence presence. In exchange, they’re offering more humanitarian aid and some sanctions relief. The catch? U.S. intelligence says there aren’t many pragmatists available. A lot of the possible replacements are even more hard-line. Source: NYT / Writer: Lynn

tweets.text: 🇺🇦🇮🇱 Zelensky basically said out loud what everyone already knows: Ukraine wants Israeli air defense badly enough to pay for it, and Israel keeps saying "we're talking" which is diplomatically saying no. tweets.creator: @MarioNawfal
tweets.text: 🇧🇬 A drone carrying a "solid amount of explosives" just entered Bulgarian airspace from Romania before crashing just 100 metres from the border. The alarming part is that Bulgaria says the drone wasn't detected by Bulgarian or Romanian radar, or even NATO's combined air operations centre. It crashed in a sunflower field near a compressor station on the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, causing no casualties or damage. Romania says its radar detected no aircraft crossing into Bulgaria, leaving the drone's origin, and how it apparently slipped through NATO air defences, unknown. Source: WarFront Witnes

Shipping companies can now reportedly send vessel details through designated contact points and arrange safe passage, while Ukrainian authorities are effectively telling operators which ships are, and aren't, fair game. Funny how everyone's fine with Ukraine doing this, but outraged with Iran doing the same in the Strait of Hormuz Source: Bloombe
